questions.stem: Each of the following is a feature of an open-end management investment company EXCEPT:
choices: It continuously offers new shares to the public
Investors purchase and redeem shares at net asset value (NAV) plus any applicable sales charge
Its shares trade in the secondary market at prices determined by supply and demand, often at a discount or premium to NAV
It may charge a 12b-1 fee to cover distribution expenses
questions.explanation: Open-end funds issue redeemable shares priced at NAV (plus any load); they do not trade in the secondary market. Shares trading at a discount or premium to NAV is characteristic of closed-end funds. 12b-1 fees and continuous offerings are open-end features.

questions.stem: A registered representative is comparing a unit investment trust (UIT) to an open-end mutual fund. Which statement is NOT accurate about the UIT?
choices: A UIT is organized under a trust indenture and has no board of directors
A UIT issues redeemable securities representing an undivided interest in a unit of specified securities
A UIT is actively managed by an investment adviser who selects and rotates the portfolio over time
A UIT is classified as an investment company under the Investment Company Act of 1940
questions.explanation: By statutory definition, a UIT has no board of directors and holds a fixed, specified portfolio—it is not actively managed. The other choices are correct features of a UIT under Section 4.

questions.stem: All of the following are characteristics common to both direct participation programs (DPPs) and non-listed REITs EXCEPT:
choices: Generally illiquid investments with limited secondary markets
Pass-through tax treatment in which losses flow through to investors at the entity level
Suitability concerns due to long holding periods
Investors purchase units or shares through a broker-dealer pursuant to a prospectus
questions.explanation: DPPs (limited partnerships) provide pass-through of both income and losses. REITs avoid double taxation by distributing income, but losses do not flow through to shareholders. Both are typically illiquid and require suitability review.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about hedge funds is LEAST accurate?
choices: They are typically structured as private partnerships
They usually require a high minimum investment and are sold to accredited or qualified investors
They are generally illiquid, often imposing lock-up periods on investors
They must redeem investor interests at NAV on a daily basis like an open-end fund
questions.explanation: Hedge funds are not open-end funds and do not provide daily redemption at NAV; they typically restrict redemptions through lock-ups and gates. The other statements correctly describe hedge funds.

questions.stem: A customer asks about municipal fund securities. Which statement is NOT correct?
choices: A 529 savings plan is a municipal fund security whose issuer would be an investment company but for Section 2(b) of the Investment Company Act of 1940
Local government investment pools (LGIPs) and ABLE accounts are categorized as municipal fund securities
529 plan assets must generally be used for qualified education expenses to retain favorable federal tax treatment
529 plan account owners must liquidate the account by the time the beneficiary reaches age 30
questions.explanation: There is no age-30 mandatory distribution requirement for 529 plans—that rule applies to Coverdell ESAs. The other choices correctly describe municipal fund securities.

questions.stem: Which of the following would MOST likely violate FINRA Rule 2342 governing breakpoint sales?
choices: A representative recommends a $24,500 mutual fund purchase when a breakpoint reduction is available at $25,000, without disclosing the breakpoint
A representative documents a bona fide asset-allocation program and discloses that the customer may forego some breakpoint reductions
A representative aggregates purchases under a written letter of intent to qualify the customer for a lower sales charge
A representative applies rights of accumulation based on the customer's existing holdings in the same fund family
questions.explanation: Selling shares in dollar amounts just below a breakpoint to capture a higher sales charge violates Rule 2342. LOI, ROA, and bona fide asset-allocation programs are permissible breakpoint-related practices.

questions.stem: Each of the following is a required suitability consideration before recommending a deferred variable annuity EXCEPT:
choices: Whether the customer would benefit from features such as tax deferral, annuitization, or a death/living benefit
Whether the customer has been informed of surrender periods and charges, mortality and expense fees, and market risk
Whether the particular contract and its subaccount allocations are suitable for the customer
Whether the contract's NAV is currently trading at a discount or premium to its market price
questions.explanation: Variable annuities are not exchange-traded securities priced at discounts or premiums to NAV. Rule 2330 requires disclosure of features, costs, and a suitability analysis covering the contract, subaccounts, and riders.

questions.stem: An investor exercises a long equity call option. Which of the following statements is correct?
choices: The resulting stock transaction settles on a T+2 basis following the exercise notice
The resulting stock transaction settles on a T+1 basis, consistent with regular-way equity settlement
The transaction settles in cash on the same business day, as with index options
Settlement does not occur until expiration of the option series
questions.explanation: Effective 5/28/2024, regular-way equity settlement is T+1, and stock delivered upon exercise of an equity option follows the same T+1 schedule. Index options settle in cash the next business day based on intrinsic value.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST distinguishes an exchange-traded note (ETN) from an exchange-traded fund (ETF)?
choices: An ETN is an unsecured debt obligation of the issuer, exposing investors to the issuer's credit risk, whereas an ETF holds a portfolio of underlying assets
Only ETNs trade on exchanges throughout the trading day
ETFs are not registered with the SEC, while ETNs are
An ETN provides voting rights in the underlying index components, while an ETF does not
questions.explanation: An ETN is a senior unsecured debt instrument whose payments depend on an index and on issuer creditworthiness. An ETF holds underlying securities. Both trade intraday on exchanges.

questions.stem: All of the following risks would be of GREATEST concern to a holder of a long-term, fixed-rate corporate bond EXCEPT:
choices: Interest rate risk
Credit risk
Purchasing power (inflation) risk
Prepayment risk
questions.explanation: Prepayment risk is principally associated with mortgage-backed securities whose underlying borrowers can repay early. Fixed-rate corporate bonds face interest rate, credit, and inflation risk; prepayment is generally not the primary concern unless the bond is callable.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about closed-end management companies is NOT correct?
choices: They issue a fixed number of shares in an IPO and the shares then trade in the secondary market
Their shares may trade at a premium or discount to NAV based on supply and demand
They are management companies under the Investment Company Act of 1940
They continuously offer and redeem shares at NAV plus any applicable sales charge
questions.explanation: Continuous issuance and redemption at NAV are features of open-end funds. Closed-end funds issue a fixed number of shares that subsequently trade on the secondary market at market-determined prices.

questions.stem: An investor wants tax-advantaged exposure to real estate income without double taxation and with daily liquidity. Which vehicle BEST meets ALL of these objectives?
choices: A non-listed (registered) REIT
A real estate limited partnership (DPP)
A listed (exchange-traded) REIT
A private REIT sold under a Regulation D exemption
questions.explanation: Listed REITs avoid entity-level taxation when distribution requirements are met, provide real estate income, and trade on exchanges providing daily liquidity. Non-listed and private REITs and real estate DPPs are illiquid; DPPs also have pass-through losses but no daily liquidity.
